notes:
Summary: enterprise evaluation focused on Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) + reliability/fallback design. Customer is mission-critical — low tolerance for availability regressions. High-level ask: predictability for sustained inference throughput, guaranteed latency SLOs, cross-region failover with minimal session loss, and clear model-variant fallback behavior when capacity is saturated.

Recent timeline: 
- 2026-02-15: 60m scoping call (Fireflies ff_20260215_ares_dedicated_eval). AE (Evan) + SE (Priya) + infra (Ares SREs). Went over current on-prem data center layout and cloud peering options.
- 2026-01-20: architecture workshop (ff_20260120_arch_workshop) — discussed KV cache replication and session affinity.
- 2025-12-05: initial intro + NDA signed; legal started export-control questionnaire.

Workload profile & targets: 
- Primary workloads: telemetry_analysis (batch + streaming), operator_chat (low-latency chat), anomaly_detection (reranking + embeddings).
- Target latency: p95 <= 200ms for short-turn chat (<=128 tokens); p95 <= 800ms for long-gen requests (<=1024 tokens). p99 targets to be negotiated.
- Throughput baseline: expect sustained 15k concurrent chat streams with median request size ~64 tokens; peak burst planning for 3x sustained.
- Availability: 99.95% SLA target (proposal), RTO/RPO for failover: RTO <= 120s for control-plane failover, expected KV-cache warm-up RPO ~30s-5m depending on session stickiness.

Dedicated capacity planning notes: 
- Preferred hardware: mixture of A100-80GB for heavy LLMs and A10G for mixed workloads. Customer asked for a recommended reserved footprint and headroom formula: baseline capacity + 30% steady-state headroom + dedicated burst pool for critical routes.
- Suggestion from SE: start with 12 A100s + 40 A10G equivalents in Dedicated pool and iterate after load testing. Plan includes autoscale floor/ceiling, but customer requires static reserved headcount for procurement.
- KV/prefix caching: need strategy for cache replication across regions (see failover section). Sticky sessions must be opt-in per route to avoid cache divergence.

Reliability & fallback design requirements (customer asks): 
- Cross-region failover: active-passive with automated health checks; warm standby region with replicated model artifacts and control-plane state. Failover playbook must include cache rehydration steps and verification hooks.
- Session affinity: preserve conversational context where possible; if session lost, fallback must provide transparent indicator to operator and optional 'replay' of last context tokens.
- Model-variant fallback: defined policy to degrade gracefully: full-precision variant -> quantized 8-bit variant -> smaller parameter-count variant -> rate-limited degraded responses. Must preserve semantic fidelity where possible.
- Routing policies: policy grammar to prefer local-region low-latency replicas, fall back to cheaper-region or smaller-model variants when Dedicated pool saturated. Customer wants explicit "quality boundary" flags returned in response metadata.

SLA negotiation items surfaced: 
- Latency SLOs by route and token-size buckets. Credits for exceeding p95/p99 thresholds at monthly granularity.
- Throughput guarantees tied to reserved GPU count and autoscale burst allowances. Clear definition of what counts as 'saturation' for credit triggers.
- Failover commitments: maximum failover window, expected request loss, and cache RPO.

Acceptance criteria / POC success metrics: 
- Throughput: sustain 150k tokens/sec across chat cluster for 1 hr with p95 latency targets met.
- Failover: scheduled region failover test with <120s control-plane failover and overall graceful degradation with less than 2% dropped sessions.
- Model fallback: under synthetic saturation, validation prompts maintain >=85% pass-rate on fidelity checks after fallback chain.
- Observability: per-route token+latency breakdown, trace IDs linking requests across failover, and postmortem artifacts for any test fail.

Operational/runbook asks: 
- Provide step-by-step failover runbook (hand-off to Ares SREs), list of required IAM roles, network CIDR ranges for peering, and KMS key rotation windows.
- Include playbook for manual promotion of warm-standby region and rollbacks if fallbacks produce unacceptable quality.

Open questions / blockers: 
- Exact procurement SKU list (customer procurement needs GPU SKUs + OPEX breakdown).
- Export-control constraints for some model weights — may require on-prem-only variants for certain workloads.
- Final SLA language for p99 latency credits (legal still reviewing).

Stubs & links: pricing + proposed capacity breakdown in Drive (drive://redwood/enterprise-deck-ares-2026.pdf). Internal ask: prepare quantified cost delta between dedicated-reserved-only vs reserved+burst-burstable.

Next actions (short): 
- SE to deliver detailed throughput SLO matrix by 2026-03-04 (Priya).
- AE to schedule cross-region dedicated demo w/ engineering on 2026-03-08 (Evan).
- Legal to provide redline SLA by 2026-03-15.
